name: Let's Seal
tagline: The open standard for proving any file is real and unaltered
description: Let's Seal is an open standard and self-hosted toolkit for proving that a file is real, unaltered, and sealed by a known certificate at a certifiable point in time. Built around the SEAL standard — Sealed Evidence Anchored to a Ledger — it is the self-hosted, open alternative to paid document-signing products. One sealed artifact has a single way to be checked and is verifiable by anyone with any conforming tool. The repository contains a certificate authority, a FastAPI signing service, a Next.js web app, a sealbot command-line tool (Node and Rust), Python and TypeScript SDKs, and a GitHub Action for sealing artifacts in CI. The hosted service at letsseal.org runs the identical code, and the standard can be self-hosted under your own certificate authority or with a commercial AATL or eIDAS certificate.
highlights: Open SEAL standard: one sealed artifact, one way to verify it, verifiable by anyone forever
Sealing APIs for PDF (PAdES), images/video/audio (C2PA), XML (XML-DSig), email (S/MIME), assets, and any file by digest
Full self-hosted stack: certificate authority, signing service, web app, CLI (Node + Rust), and SDKs
Bitcoin anchoring for time-proof of existence
GitHub Action to seal artifacts directly in CI pipelines
curatorNote: Let's Seal frames itself as 'Let's Encrypt for document signing' — it wants to make proving a file is authentic a public good rather than a paid service. It earned 94 HN points in-window yet remains tiny, and the self-hosted, open-standard angle is a genuinely novel niche.
